question: European Court of Auditors Special Report 22/2023 on ‘Offshore renewable energy in the EU’1 contains a number of recommendations. In particular, the Court calls on the Commission to assist Member States in assessing ‘the potential employment, skills and social implications of [offshore renewable energy] development in the offshore energy sector and for other users of the sea, notably fisheries’ (see Recommendation 2). 1.
Has the Commission already implemented this recommendation, in particular as regards the fisheries sector? If so, could it provide feedback on this matter?
If not, how does it plan to proceed with implementing this recommendation by the end of 2025 (deadline advised by the Court of Auditors)?
European Court of Auditors Special Report 22/2023 on ‘Offshore renewable energy in the EU’
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.1.2025) Following the European Court of Auditors’ (ECA) recommendation1 to assess the potential employment, skills and social implications of developments in the offshore renewable energy sector and for other users of the sea, notably fisheries, the Commission has launched a call for tender to analyse these aspects in detail.

The contractor has been selected, and the kick off meeting took place in August 2024. The scope of the study will cover the topics raised by ECA in the recommendation, with a specific focus on the fisheries sector. The final report is expected by August 2025.
